items.stem: Which organisms occupy the first trophic level in all food chains?
items.markingKey: (c) producers.

items.stem: In the food chain grass → goat → human, what is the role of the human?
items.markingKey: (b) Position 3 in the chain: secondary consumer.

items.stem: Why do food chains usually have only three or four trophic levels?
items.answer: Only about 10% of energy passes to the next level, so very little energy is left after four levels.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Classify these organisms as a herbivore or a carnivore: a grasshopper, a lion, a deer, a tiger, a rabbit.
items.answer: A herbivore: a deer, a grasshopper, a rabbit. A carnivore: a lion, a tiger.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A herbivore: a deer, a grasshopper, a rabbit. A carnivore: a lion, a tiger.

items.stem: Arrange these into a food chain: snake, grass, insects, peacock, lizard. Name the producer and the top consumer.
items.answer: grass → insects → lizard → snake → peacock; producer: grass; top consumer: peacock
items.markingKey: Start with the producer and follow "is eaten by".

items.stem:
Read: A student studying a grassland near Kanha recorded the food chain wheat → mouse → snake → hawk. The producers (wheat) capture 50000 kJ of solar energy.
(i) Which organism is the producer, and which is the top consumer? (ii) How much energy reaches the snake? (iii) If a pesticide is sprayed on the wheat, which organism will have the highest concentration of it? (iv) Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five levels?
items.answer: (i) Wheat; hawk. (ii) 500 kJ. (iii) The hawk (biological magnification). (iv) Only about 10% of energy passes to each next level, so little energy remains.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Classify these organisms as a producer or a decomposer: bacteria in the soil, grass, phytoplankton, a mushroom.
items.answer: A producer: grass, phytoplankton. A decomposer: a mushroom, bacteria in the soil.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A producer: grass, phytoplankton. A decomposer: a mushroom, bacteria in the soil.

items.stem:
Read: A student studying a grassland near Kanha recorded the food chain plants → rabbit → fox → wolf. The producers (plants) capture 50000 kJ of solar energy.
(i) Which organism is the producer, and which is the top consumer? (ii) How much energy reaches the fox? (iii) If a pesticide is sprayed on the plants, which organism will have the highest concentration of it? (iv) Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five levels?
items.answer: (i) Plants; wolf. (ii) 500 kJ. (iii) The wolf (biological magnification). (iv) Only about 10% of energy passes to each next level, so little energy remains.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: A student studying a grassland near Kanha recorded the food chain algae → water flea → small fish → crane. The producers (algae) capture 20000 kJ of solar energy.
(i) Which organism is the producer, and which is the top consumer? (ii) How much energy reaches the small fish? (iii) If a pesticide is sprayed on the algae, which organism will have the highest concentration of it? (iv) Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five levels?
items.answer: (i) Algae; crane. (ii) 200 kJ. (iii) The crane (biological magnification). (iv) Only about 10% of energy passes to each next level, so little energy remains.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: If all the snakes in a grassland were killed, what would happen to the populations of frogs, grasshoppers and grass? Explain.
items.answer: Frogs would increase (no predator), grasshoppers would decrease (more frogs eat them), and grass might increase; the ecosystem balance is upset.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.markingKey: (b) Bacteria in the soil is a decomposer. The others: algae – a producer; phytoplankton – a producer; an eagle – a carnivore.

items.stem:
Read: A student studying a grassland near Kanha recorded the food chain phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → large fish → kingfisher. The producers (phytoplankton) capture 20000 kJ of solar energy.
(i) Which organism is the producer, and which is the top consumer? (ii) How much energy reaches the small fish? (iii) If a pesticide is sprayed on the phytoplankton, which organism will have the highest concentration of it? (iv) Why do food chains rarely have more than four or five levels?
items.answer: (i) Phytoplankton; kingfisher. (ii) 200 kJ. (iii) The kingfisher (biological magnification). (iv) Only about 10% of energy passes to each next level, so little energy remains.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Classify these organisms as a producer or a carnivore: phytoplankton, algae, a tiger, a snake.

items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A producer: algae, phytoplankton. A carnivore: a snake, a tiger.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The flow of energy in a food chain is unidirectional.
Reason (R): Energy captured by plants does not return to the Sun.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "All the interacting organisms in an area together with the non-living components of their environment."

items.stem: What is meant by the 10 percent law?
items.answer: The rule that only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The 10 percent law – the rule that only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next.

items.stem: In the food chain phytoplankton → zooplankton → small fish → large fish → kingfisher, the producers (phytoplankton) capture 5000 kJ of energy. Using the 10 percent law, how much energy is available to the kingfisher?
items.markingKey: (d) Each transfer passes on 10%: 5000 × (0.1)^4 = 0.5 kJ.

items.stem: Why are human beings at the highest risk of biological magnification?
items.answer: Humans occupy the top level in many food chains, so harmful chemicals accumulate most in our bodies.

items.stem: Why is the flow of energy in an ecosystem described as unidirectional?
items.answer: Energy moves from the Sun to producers and then to consumers; it is lost as heat at each level and does not return to the previous level.

items.stem: A food chain has a top carnivore receiving 20 kJ. If the chain has four trophic levels, how much energy did the producer capture, and what happens to the rest?

items.markingKey: 1 mark calculation. 1 mark 10% law. 1 mark heat loss.

items.stem: What is meant by the Kyoto Protocol?

items.stem: Suggest two changes in your habits to reduce the problem of waste disposal.
items.answer: Carry a cloth bag instead of polythene; compost kitchen waste; reuse containers; avoid disposable items.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each (any two).

items.stem: Yash's family of 5 produces 0.4 kg of waste per person per day, of which 65% is biodegradable. How much non-biodegradable waste do they produce in 30 days, and what should they do with it?
items.answer: 21 kg; segregate it and send it for recycling (reduce and reuse plastics)
items.markingKey: Total = 5 × 0.4 × 30 = 60 kg; non-biodegradable = 35% = 21 kg.

items.stem: A town decides to ban single-use plastic bags. Give two environmental benefits and suggest two alternatives.
